docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
PorosData is a scientific document processing and structured delivery framework. It turns PDFs, OCR outputs, and parser results into data assets that are easier to review, reuse, and deliver downstream.

In empirical research domains such as materials science, source documents often contain broken numbers, spacing noise, term corruption, damaged formulas, and disconnected figure references. These issues quickly affect model training, structured extraction, retrieval workflows, and manual review. PorosData is designed to reduce that noise and produce stable, traceable deliverables.

docs.title: Where It Fits
docs.text:
PorosData fits the stage between raw literature inputs and delivery-ready data assets.

  • Prepare research literature for model training
  • Provide stable inputs for structured extraction, rule-based processing, and semantic retrieval
  • Organize body text, captions, tables, and image assets into one delivery layout
  • Support downstream database building, knowledge organization, and multimodal use

docs.title: Core Value
docs.text:
PorosData follows Academic Atomicity, which means improving usability without stripping away the scientific meaning of the source material.

Dimension Value Reliable Content Formulas, citations, units, and terms are kept as intact as possible Clear Structure Sections, text blocks, figures, and fields become easier for both systems and reviewers to follow Traceable Process The path from raw input to delivered output remains inspectable Reusable Delivery One output set can support training, extraction, retrieval, and storage workflows

docs.title: Product Framework
docs.text:
PorosData uses a three-stage pipeline for scientific documents:

The diagram below shows how storage, processing modules, and delivery-facing outputs are connected in one end-to-end system.

[Raw Literature] -> Parser -> Processor -> Designer -> [Training Text / Structured Outputs / Multimodal Index]
Module What It Delivers Parser Extracts reusable text blocks and assets from PDFs and parser outputs Processor Cleans noise, repairs fragmentation, and stabilizes terms and numerical expressions Designer Reorganizes quality-ready text into full-text views, extraction-ready outputs, and multimodal indexes

docs.title: Capability Overview
docs.text: Capability Problem It Solves Intelligent text cleaning Control characters, index noise, token fragmentation, and broken words Scientific term validation OCR-driven term corruption such as X-ray -> 10-ray Numerical and unit repair Broken scientific notation, decimal points, and units Entity stabilization Chemical elements and material names misread as LaTeX or symbols Asset anchoring Cross-modal indexing between figure references, images, and captions

docs.title: Final Deliverables
docs.text:
PorosData does not stop at producing cleaner text. A standard delivery package typically includes:

  • Full-text outputs for reading and review
  • Plain-text streams for training use
  • Structured JSON outputs for extraction and retrieval
  • Multimodal indexes that connect text references with image assets
  • Reports and logs for batch review and delivery traceability

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text:
This page explains the PorosData roadmap from an external delivery perspective. It focuses on two questions:

  • what the product can already deliver today
  • how the final delivery package will be expanded over time

docs.title: Product Framework
docs.text:
PorosData is organized around one continuous delivery chain:

Module Current Role Main Output Parser receives raw papers and upstream parser results reusable text blocks, image assets, and basic metadata Processor prepares content quality cleaned intermediate outputs, processing reports, stable inputs Designer builds delivery-ready structure full-text outputs, structured JSON, multimodal indexes

These layers are designed to work together as one delivery system: preserve the source package, stabilize content quality, and then organize the final outputs.

docs.title: Final Delivery Package
docs.text:
The target delivery package includes:

  • a result directory organized by document ID
  • plain-text outputs for training preparation
  • structured outputs for extraction, retrieval, and storage
  • multimodal indexes that keep text and image references connected
  • reports that support review and traceability

docs.title: Phase 1: Current Deliverables
docs.text:
The current stage focuses on making the full pipeline operational for batch use:

  • end-to-end processing from raw literature to final delivery directories
  • three core output groups: full-text, structured results, and multimodal indexes
  • a standard raw -> processed -> structured directory model
  • baseline audit, validation, and batch reporting support
  • an early delivery loop of process -> review -> correction -> rerun

docs.title: Phase 2: Near-Term Improvements
docs.text:
The near-term goal is to make outputs more stable and easier to adopt in production projects:

  • further unify terms, units, citations, and section organization
  • improve stability for long documents, complex formulas, and larger batch jobs
  • expand deployment guides, usage guides, and result interpretation documents for external users
  • strengthen figure-text linking and review workflows
  • gradually formalize suspicious-pattern feedback and rule updates

docs.title: Phase 3: Final Product Shape
docs.text:
The final goal is a more complete scientific document delivery product:

  • clearer standards for batch delivery and result acceptance
  • one consistent delivery model across full-text, structured, and multimodal outputs
  • stable reuse of outputs for training, extraction, retrieval, and storage
  • better project-level tracking, review, and iterative improvement

  • project teams preparing scientific literature datasets
  • engineering teams building training corpora

docs.title: Design Philosophy
docs.text:
The core idea behind PorosData is simple: scientific literature is not ordinary text. It carries terms, units, formulas, figures, and contextual relations that must survive processing if the result is meant to stay useful.

The value of the system is not in rewriting papers into simpler language. It is in making them more stable, more structured, and easier to use downstream without losing scientific meaning.

docs.title: Pillar One: Academic Atomicity
docs.text: PorosData treats each piece of scientific content as a unit that should not be broken apart carelessly. Processing should preserve meaning, physical constraints, and contextual relations as much as possible.

docs.title: Character Level
docs.text: Formulas, chemical expressions, and special symbols should not be structurally damaged by processing steps.

docs.title: Relation Level
docs.text: Numbers, units, experimental conditions, and conclusions should remain connected during cleaning and reorganization.

docs.title: Structure Level
docs.text: Section hierarchy, figure references, and key context should remain traceable and understandable in the final outputs.

docs.title: Pillar Two: Knowledge-Constrained Processing
docs.text: PorosData does not treat scientific content as plain strings alone. It applies domain-aware constraints when normalizing and organizing data.

docs.title: Rules Should Serve Meaning
docs.text: Term normalization, unit consistency, citation cleanup, and chemical-expression protection are used to keep outputs closer to the intended scientific meaning, not just to make formatting look cleaner.

docs.title: Experience Should Become Reusable
docs.text: Domain experience should be turned into reusable processing strategies so batch workflows can follow a more stable standard.

docs.title: Pillar Three: Layered Delivery
docs.text: PorosData uses a layered delivery chain instead of trying to solve every problem in one step.

docs.title: Parser
docs.text: Keep as much usable content and as many source assets as possible from the original literature.

docs.title: Processor
docs.text: Resolve quality issues first so text, captions, and key fields become stable enough for further use.

docs.title: Designer
docs.text: Then organize those stable inputs into full-text, structured, and multimodal outputs for final delivery.

docs.title: Vision
docs.text: PorosData aims to provide a practical delivery chain for scientific literature, so papers can move more smoothly into training, extraction, retrieval, and review workflows while preserving the rigor expected in research communication.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: This page collects the core terms used across the PorosData documentation so readers can move between workflow, tool, and delivery pages with one shared vocabulary.

docs.title: Parser
docs.text: The upstream extraction stage that turns raw papers into reusable text blocks, figures, captions, and metadata.

docs.title: Processor
docs.text: The quality-preparation stage that cleans noisy parser outputs and makes them stable enough for downstream use.

docs.title: Designer
docs.text: The structured-delivery stage that organizes stable inputs into full-text outputs, structured JSON, and multimodal indexes.

docs.title: raw
docs.text: The source layer that keeps original papers and upstream parser results for traceability.

docs.title: processed
docs.text: The intermediate layer that stores cleaned outputs and processing reports.

docs.title: structured
docs.text: The final delivery layer that stores full-text results, extraction-ready outputs, and multimodal assets.

docs.title: full_text
docs.text: The delivery form used for readable and reviewable full-document outputs.

docs.title: datamining
docs.text: The delivery form used for structured extraction, retrieval, and storage-oriented workflows.

docs.title: multimodal
docs.text: The delivery form used to connect figure references in text with image assets and related descriptions.

docs.title: doc_id
docs.text: The document identifier used to organize outputs and keep the delivery structure consistent.

docs.title: Caption
docs.text: The descriptive text attached to a figure or table and often required for downstream review and extraction.

docs.title: Asset Anchor
docs.text: A stable reference that links a figure or table mention in text to the actual asset in the delivery package.

docs.title: processing_report
docs.text: The batch summary file that records output status, progress signals, and quality-review clues.

docs.title: Academic Atomicity
docs.text: The principle that scientific meaning, structural cues, and context should remain as intact as possible during processing.

docs.title: PorosData Workflow: From Raw Papers to Final Deliverables
docs.text: This page explains how PorosData turns scientific literature into outputs that are ready for training, structured extraction, retrieval, and human review. The focus here is the delivery path, not a single code example.

docs.title: Pipeline Overview
docs.text:
Raw Literature -> Parser -> Processor -> Designer -> Final Delivery Package

Stage Main Task Output Parser Extract text blocks, figures, captions, and basic metadata Reusable raw content and image assets Processor Remove noise, repair fragmentation, and normalize expressions Quality-ready intermediate results and reports Designer Organize sections and export structured views and indexes Full-text outputs, structured JSON, and multimodal assets

docs.title: Input and Output Layout
docs.text:
PorosData works best with a three-layer directory structure:

data/
├── raw/          # upstream parser results
├── processed/    # cleaned intermediate results
└── structured/   # final delivery package

The standard data flow is raw -> processed -> structured.

docs.title: Stage 1: Raw Inputs in raw
docs.text:
The raw layer keeps the upstream source package intact. Typical contents include:

  • Original PDF files
  • Parser-generated Markdown or content lists
  • Page-level intermediate files
  • Extracted image assets

This layer is preserved for traceability and review rather than for direct downstream delivery.

docs.title: Stage 2: Processor Builds processed
docs.text:
Processor turns raw parser results into stable intermediate inputs. Typical issues handled at this stage include:

  • Numbers, decimal points, and units broken by spacing noise
  • Fragmented or corrupted terms, material names, and chemical expressions
  • Noisy captions, table titles, and footnotes
  • Long text blocks polluted by control characters or formatting artifacts

Standard outputs at this stage usually include:

  • Cleaned *_content_list.json
  • Reusable copies of image assets
  • A processing report such as processing_report.json

docs.title: Stage 3: Designer Builds structured
docs.text:
Designer converts quality-ready inputs into final delivery outputs. A typical result layout is:

data/structured/
├── full_text/
├── datamining/
└── multimodal/

These three output groups serve different downstream needs:

Directory Purpose Common Files full_text/ Readable and reviewable full-text delivery _structured.json, _structured.txt datamining/ Extraction-ready and retrieval-ready structured outputs _datamining.json multimodal/ Indexed image assets linked back to the text _index.json, fig_*.md, assets/

docs.title: What Users Receive
docs.text:
After a standard run, users typically receive:

  1. A delivery directory organized by document ID
  2. Plain-text outputs suitable for training use
  3. Structured outputs suitable for extraction and retrieval
  4. Multimodal indexes that connect text references to image assets
  5. Reports that support batch review and delivery tracking

docs.title: Recommended Reading Order
docs.text:
For batch projects, the easiest way to review results is:

  1. Start with raw/ and confirm the source package is complete
  2. Check processed/ and its report to confirm the cleaning stage completed cleanly
  3. Open structured/ and choose the full-text, structured, or multimodal outputs based on your downstream task

docs.text:
• Prepare high-quality text for training workflows
  • Provide stable inputs for structured extraction
  • Create indexable links between figures and body text
  • Deliver one consistent package for database building and knowledge organization

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Install PorosData in the way that best fits your workflow: quick local evaluation, source-based development, or long-running server execution.

docs.title: Recommended Method
docs.text:
For most users, start with the published package:

pip install porosdata-processor

This is the fastest way to verify the basic text-processing capability and run small local tests.

docs.title: Install from Source
docs.text:
If you need to inspect the codebase, adjust processing behavior, or test local changes, install from source:

git clone https://github.com/KiventYip/porosdata-processor.git
cd porosdata-processor
pip install -e .

For development environments, you can install the extended dependency set if it is available in the repository configuration.

docs.title: Environment Notes
docs.text:
Before installation, make sure the environment meets these basic requirements:

  • Python 3.8+
  • a writable local environment or virtual environment
  • enough disk space for raw, processed, and structured outputs

For larger batch projects, Linux plus SSD or NVMe storage is recommended.

docs.title: Verify the Installation
docs.text:
After installation, confirm that the package is available:

import porosdata_processor
print(porosdata_processor.__version__)

If you plan to run batch jobs, also verify the command-line entry:

python -m porosdata_processor --help

docs.title: What to Prepare Next
docs.text:
After installation, prepare three things before your first run:

  1. raw source documents or upstream parser results
  2. a target output location for processed results
  3. a small validation sample before launching a full batch

docs.title: Clean Text
docs.text:
Use TextCleaner to normalize scientific text while preserving formulas:

from porosdata_processor import TextCleaner

# Initialize cleaner with default settings
cleaner = TextCleaner()

# Process text
raw_text = "The energy equation is $E = mc^2$, involving α particles and β rays."
cleaned_text = cleaner.clean(raw_text)

print(cleaned_text)
# Output: "The energy equation is $E = mc^2$, involving \alpha particles and \beta rays."

docs.title: Custom Pipeline
docs.text:
Configure a cleaner with specific plugins:

# Create a cleaner with specific plugins
cleaner = TextCleaner(pipeline=[
    "citation_rules",      # Normalize citations
    "greek_to_latex",      # Convert Greek letters
    "normalize_whitespace" # Clean up spacing
])

text = "See reference 【1】 for α particle data."
result = cleaner.clean(text)
# Output: "See reference [1] for \alpha particle data."

docs.title: Advanced Options
docs.text:
Enable advanced LaTeX formula cleaning:

# Enable advanced LaTeX formula cleaning
cleaner = TextCleaner(clean_options={
    "clean_latex_math_spaces": True  # Remove extra spaces inside formulas
})

text = "Formula: $\\mathbf { X } + \\frac { a }{ b }$"
result = cleaner.clean(text)
# Output: "Formula: $\\mathbf{X} + \\frac{a}{b}$"

docs.title: Process Single File
docs.text:
# Clean a Markdown file
cleaner.clean_file(
    input_path="document.md",
    output_path="clean_document.md",
    encoding="utf-8"
)

docs.title: Batch Processing
docs.text:
from processing.batch_processor import BatchProcessor

processor = BatchProcessor()
processor.process_text_data(
    input_dir="data/raw",
    output_dir="data/cleaned"
)

docs.title: Processing Configuration
docs.text:
Create a config/processing_config.yaml:

cleaning:
  convert_greek: true
  apply_rules: true
  apply_patterns: true
  normalize_whitespace: true
  remove_extra_spaces: true

processing:
  concurrency: 0  # 0 for sequential processing
  verbose: true

docs.title: Token Configuration
docs.text:
For advanced tokenization settings, create config/token_config.yaml:

model_type: "llama"  # or "gpt", "custom"

tokens:
  llama:
    bos: "<s>"
    eos: "</s>"
    inst_start: "[INST]"
    inst_end: "[/INST]"

splitting:
  max_chunk_tokens: 512
  split_by_paragraph: true
  preserve_paragraphs: true
  overlap_tokens: 50

docs.title: Processor API Overview
docs.text:
This page is a practical reference entry for the current processing-facing interfaces. It is intended to answer three questions quickly:

  • what to call
  • what to pass in
  • what to expect back

docs.title: Scope of This Page
docs.text:
The current repository documentation is centered on the processing layer. In practice, the public-facing entry points fall into four groups:

Area Responsibility Typical Entry Processor text cleaning and quality preparation TextCleaner, CLI run batch processing process multiple source documents into processed outputs python -m porosdata_processor run review and acceptance inspect processed outputs before handoff audit and delivery-gate style commands Designer handoff take stable processed results into final delivery outputs documented as a downstream stage, not a primary API in this page

If you are looking for final structured delivery outputs, start with the Designer documentation after the processing stage is complete.

docs.title: Typical Call Path
docs.text:
The most common usage path is:

Raw paper or parser output
-> TextCleaner or batch run
-> processed outputs
-> review and acceptance
-> downstream structured delivery

docs.title: TextCleaner
docs.text: Use TextCleaner when you want to clean one piece of scientific text inside Python code.

docs.title: Constructor
docs.text:
TextCleaner(pipeline=None, clean_options=None)
Parameter Type Meaning pipeline list | None ordered list of cleaning plugins clean_options dict | None additional cleaning switches

docs.title: clean(text)
docs.text:
Clean one text string with the configured pipeline.

Item Value Input text: str Return str Use case inline cleaning, local testing, rule verification 
from porosdata_processor import TextCleaner

cleaner = TextCleaner()
result = cleaner.clean("The α phase appears in Fig. 1.")
print(result)

docs.title: clean_file(input_path, output_path, encoding="utf-8")
docs.text:
Clean one file and write the result to disk.

Parameter Type Meaning input_path str source file path output_path str target file path encoding str file encoding, default utf-8 Return Meaning written file cleaned file output at output_path

docs.title: Batch CLI
docs.text: Use the CLI when you want to process a directory instead of one text string.

docs.title: Typical Command
docs.text:
python -m porosdata_processor run \
  --input-dir data/raw \
  --output-dir data/processed \
  --max-workers 4

docs.title: Input and Output
docs.text: Item Meaning --input-dir source directory with raw or upstream parser outputs --output-dir target directory for processed results --max-workers batch concurrency for multi-file runs Output Meaning cleaned content lists quality-ready intermediate outputs copied assets reusable image assets processing_report.json batch summary for review

docs.title: Review and Acceptance Commands
docs.text: Use these commands when the batch is complete and you need to inspect whether the outputs are ready to hand off.

docs.title: Quality Review
docs.text:
python -m porosdata_processor audit \
  --processed-dir data/processed \
  --report-file docs/audit/aiready_data_audit_result.json

docs.title: Delivery Gate
docs.text:
python -m porosdata_processor delivery-gate \
  --processed-dir data/processed \
  --report-file docs/audit/delivery_gate_report.md \
  --json-file docs/audit/delivery_gate_result.json

These commands are most useful in project handoff, batch review, or recurring quality checks.

docs.title: Parameters and Behavior at a Glance
Common Processing Options
docs.text: Option Where It Appears Meaning pipeline TextCleaner(...) choose or order cleaning plugins clean_options TextCleaner(...) enable or tune specific cleaning behavior --input-dir CLI source data location --output-dir CLI processed output location --max-workers CLI number of parallel workers

docs.title: Expected Return Types
docs.text: Entry Returns or Produces clean(text) one cleaned string clean_file(...) one cleaned file run processed directory outputs and batch report audit review report delivery-gate acceptance report and machine-readable result

docs.title: Exceptions and Failure Signals
docs.text:
The Python API may raise runtime exceptions when configuration or processing is invalid. The two most common documented categories are:

Exception Meaning Typical Cause ProcessingError text processing failed invalid input, unsupported text case, or processing failure ConfigurationError configuration is invalid wrong option shape or unsupported config value 
try:
    cleaner = TextCleaner()
    result = cleaner.clean(text)
except ProcessingError as e:
    print(f"Processing failed: {e}")
except ConfigurationError as e:
    print(f"Configuration error: {e}")

For batch runs, the main failure signals are more often found in logs, processing reports, and delivery-gate outputs than in a direct Python exception.

docs.title: Design Insights
docs.text:
Quick Links: Home | Quick Start

To ensure that scientific data can truly support model training and scientific data mining, PorosData follows a data-processing standard centered on semantic stability, structural consistency, and minability.

Different downstream scenarios impose different quality requirements. The two most central scenarios are:

  • Pre-training: learning world knowledge and language structure
  • Automated Data Mining: extracting structured knowledge from large-scale scientific literature

docs.title: Document Placement
docs.text:
This page serves as a research-level overview and technical-path discussion. The concrete engineering constraints have been absorbed into the two tool pages in the current documentation structure:

  • Processor: see tools/processor/index.md, focused on data quality delivery, cleaning standards, and entry conditions for Designer
  • Designer: see tools/designer/index.md, focused on structured views, Poros tag contracts, and data-mining delivery standards

docs.title: 1. Data Cleaning Capability (PorosData Processor)
docs.text:
At the pre-training stage, text is consumed as token sequences. The goal is to let the model learn world knowledge and linguistic structure. If raw data contains noise or errors, the model may learn false statistical correlations and fail to understand scientific concepts. Therefore, training-ready data must satisfy three baseline properties before entering pre-training: token purity, terminology accuracy, and structural coherence.

First, the token stream must remain pure. Text converted from PDFs or OCR often contains non-semantic artifacts such as control symbols, page indices, or formatting residue. These fragments do not belong to grammar or meaning, but language models still tokenize them as ordinary input, disturbing contextual probability learning. Such noise must therefore be detected and removed.

Second, scientific terminology must remain semantically accurate. Scientific terms are highly stable semantic units. If parsing introduces systematic corruption, the model learns wrong knowledge. For example, if X-ray is misread as 10-ray, the scientific concept itself is damaged. Domain dictionaries and contextual rules are therefore necessary to protect critical scientific terms from incorrect substitution.

Third, long-text structure must remain coherent. In PDF parsing, broken words and missing hyphens across line breaks are common. For example, short-range may be split into short - range, or collapsed into shortrange. Such damage increases vocabulary uncertainty and breaks stable terminology into meaningless tokens. This cleaning stage restores word continuity and hyphen structure so that the model can learn long and complex scientific sentences more reliably.

docs.title: 2. Structured Data Capability (PorosData Designer)
docs.text:
Unlike pre-training, the goal of data mining is to extract structured knowledge from scientific literature, such as material composition, experimental conditions, or physical parameters. In this setting, the key requirement is no longer language fluency, but stable entity recognition, accurate numerical expression, and alignment between text and multimodal assets.

First, numerical values and units must remain determinate. Key scientific knowledge is often expressed numerically, such as temperature, pressure, or material properties. During OCR, exponent forms and digit sequences are often broken apart, for example $10^5$ becoming $1 0 ^ { 5 }$. Such corruption prevents automated mining systems from recognizing the correct magnitude, and directly damages downstream extraction. The processing pipeline must therefore restore scientific notation and exponent structures into standardized form.

Second, entity recognition must remain stable. Scientific documents depend heavily on chemical elements and material names such as Ni, Au, or Fe3C. If these are misread into LaTeX-like commands or malformed symbol structures, downstream NER and entity linking fail, and knowledge graph entities cannot be built correctly. The processing pipeline therefore needs rule and dictionary protection for scientific entities.

Third, multimodal assets must be anchorable. Important information in scientific papers often exists not only in the main text, but also in figures, tables, and images. Traditional text parsing often preserves only string mentions like Fig. 1 or Table 2, without building a direct connection to the actual assets. The processing pipeline should convert those mentions into indexable structural anchors, so the textual reference can directly point to the corresponding figure asset and caption. This text-image linkage is foundational for multimodal knowledge mining and scientific document understanding.

docs.title: Panorama of Technical Paths for Scientific Data Processing
1. Regex: the Low-Level Sweeper
docs.text: Dimension Description Core Logic Hard-coded rule matching based on patterns Typical Cases Physical-unit concatenation (3 m m -> 3mm), broken decimals (0 . 1 -> 0.1), page-header and page-number noise removal Advantages Extremely fast, deterministic, and nearly free computationally Limitations Cannot resolve ambiguity well, for example whether Ni- should be merged or treated as a minus sign Contribution Improves the signal-to-noise ratio and reduces wasted tokens

docs.title: 2. Glossaries and Dictionaries: the Domain Defense Line
docs.text: Dimension Description Core Logic Multi-pattern matching, such as Aho-Corasick, to force fragmented OCR strings into professional terminology Typical Cases Chemical elements (Z r -> Zr), material abbreviations (B M G -> BMG), instrument names Advantages Strongly improves entity stability and protects critical scientific data Limitations Expensive to maintain and weak on genuinely new compounds or novel materials outside the dictionary Data Mining Contribution Essential for entity normalization, knowledge graph construction, and attribute extraction

docs.title: 3. OCR Model Selection: Source-Level Suppression
docs.text: Dimension Description Core Logic Shift from character recognition to visual-semantic understanding Representative Tools Traditional OCR such as PaddleOCR and Tesseract, which often break formulas and chemistry notation; vision-formula models such as Nougat and Marker, which directly predict Markdown or LaTeX sequences from academic PDFs Advantages Better recovery of tables, formulas, and multi-column layouts Limitations Requires more compute and may hallucinate missing segments on irregular layouts Contribution Produces structured text closer to the source and skips a large share of downstream regex cleanup

docs.title: 4. Small-Model Finetuning or Polishing: Semantic Final Correction
docs.text: Dimension Description Core Logic Use 1B-3B scale models such as Qwen or Llama through prompting or supervised finetuning for semantic correction Typical Cases Complex OCR artifacts that are not fixed patterns, such as malformed symbol sequences around chemical terms Advantages Brings semantic commonsense into the loop and can infer likely scientific corrections Limitations Slower, and must be tightly controlled so the original meaning is corrected rather than rewritten Contribution Pushes text quality closer to publication-grade language and improves embedding retrieval quality

docs.title: Comparative Summary
docs.text: Approach Cost Flexibility Accuracy Core Goal Regex Very low Low Very high for known patterns Remove physical noise such as spacing and formatting artifacts Dictionary attachment Low Medium Near-perfect inside the dictionary scope Normalize entities such as material names and formulas OCR model selection Medium to high High High for academic PDFs Restore structural content such as formulas and tables Small-model finetuning High Very high Very high with semantic context Final semantic-level correction

docs.title: Current Limits
docs.text:

  • how to repair difficult formulas without over-correcting them
  • how to keep terminology dictionaries broad enough without making them too expensive to maintain
  • how to preserve stable anchors across different parser outputs
  • how to balance throughput, precision, and review cost in large delivery batches

docs.title: Problem Background
docs.text:
Scientific literature is rich in terminology, numbers, formulas, figures, and contextual qualifiers. Once papers are converted from PDF or OCR outputs into machine-readable text, small formatting errors quickly become downstream data problems.

Typical failures include:

  • broken numbers and units
  • corrupted scientific terms
  • damaged formula boundaries
  • captions and figure references losing their links
  • context such as temperature, condition, or method drifting away from the value it describes

Because of this, scientific data preparation needs a different quality standard from general-purpose text processing.

docs.title: Why Training Preparation and Data Mining Need Different Standards
docs.text: The two major downstream scenarios care about different failure modes.

docs.title: 1. Training Preparation
docs.text:
Training preparation is sensitive to sequence quality and semantic continuity.

  • Token purity matters because control characters, page residue, and non-semantic fragments waste sequence budget and disturb learning.
  • Terminology accuracy matters because corrupted terms such as X-ray -> 10-ray teach the wrong concept.
  • Long-text coherence matters because broken words and damaged punctuation reduce the stability of long scientific passages.

docs.title: 2. Data Mining
docs.text:
Data mining is sensitive to structural precision and contextual binding.

  • Values and units must stay determinate, or downstream extraction cannot recover the right magnitude.
  • Entity names must stay stable, or matching, linking, and normalization become unreliable.
  • Text-image anchors must remain explicit, or figures and captions cannot be reused in structured delivery.

docs.title: Where PorosData Fits
docs.text:
PorosData addresses these two scenarios through a layered delivery chain:

Stage Main Responsibility Why It Matters Parser preserve usable source content and assets keeps the source package intact enough for later recovery Processor remove noise and stabilize text quality prepares content for reliable downstream use Designer export delivery-ready structures turns stable inputs into full-text, structured, and multimodal outputs

In other words, PorosData does not treat cleaning and delivery as separate concerns. It treats them as one connected path from source material to reusable outputs.

docs.title: What Kind of Data Quality Do We Need?
docs.text: The target quality profile can be summarized in two views.

docs.title: Training Preparation View
docs.text:
• the text should be readable and structurally continuous
  • scientific terms should stay semantically correct
  • formulas and inline references should remain intact enough for downstream use

docs.title: Data Mining View
docs.text:
• values, units, and attributes should remain identifiable
  • entities should stay stable within and across documents
  • figure references, captions, and other metadata should remain connected to the main text

docs.title: Current Limits and Open Questions
docs.text:
Even with a stable processing pipeline, several questions remain open:

  • how far should automatic repair go before it risks changing source meaning
  • how should highly irregular formulas be normalized without damaging structure
  • how much domain dictionary coverage is enough before maintenance cost becomes too high
  • how should multimodal anchoring be kept stable across different parser outputs

These are not just implementation details. They directly affect whether a delivery package remains reusable across projects.

docs.title: Positioning
docs.text:
Designer is the structured-delivery module in PorosData. It works on top of the quality-prepared output from Processor and turns text, figures, and context into final deliverables that support training, extraction, retrieval, and review.

In short:

  • Processor makes the content stable
  • Designer organizes it into delivery-ready outputs

docs.title: Main Responsibilities
docs.text:
Designer focuses on:

  • section and paragraph organization
  • structured field assembly
  • text-image linking
  • export of full-text and structured outputs
  • multimodal index generation

It is not intended to take over large-scale OCR cleaning. Its role is to turn already-stable intermediate inputs into usable delivery products.

docs.title: Three Core Output Groups
docs.text:
At the current stage, Designer mainly delivers three output groups:

Output Group Main Use Common Files Full-text outputs reading, review, training preparation _structured.txt, _structured.json Structured outputs extraction, retrieval, storage _datamining.json Multimodal outputs figure-text linking and asset management _index.json, fig_*.md, assets/

docs.title: Output Layout
docs.text:
A typical output layout looks like this:

data/structured/
├── full_text/{doc_id}/
├── datamining/{doc_id}/
└── multimodal/{doc_id}/

Each document is stored by doc_id, which makes batch delivery, spot checks, and backtracking easier.

docs.title: What Users Receive
docs.text:
In a standard delivery run, Designer organizes one paper into several reusable result types:

  • a readable full-text result
  • a plain-text stream for training use
  • a structured JSON result for extraction and retrieval
  • a multimodal index that links text references back to image assets

docs.title: full_text
docs.text:
full_text is the full-document delivery layer and usually includes:

  • a complete text with structural markers
  • a plain-text stream without those markers
  • a human-readable text version for inspection

docs.title: datamining
docs.text:
datamining is the structured-use layer and usually includes:

  • title
  • section content
  • formula lists
  • chemical or material expressions
  • figure and table references

docs.title: multimodal
docs.text:
multimodal is the figure-linking layer and usually includes:

  • an image index file
  • figure-level description cards
  • image assets connected to text references

docs.title: Input Expectations
docs.text:
To produce stable outputs, Designer expects:

  • major noise has already been handled upstream
  • numbers, units, terms, and material names are reasonably consistent
  • captions, table titles, and footnotes are already usable
  • text-to-figure references have not been broken earlier in the pipeline

docs.title: Design Principles
docs.text:
Designer follows a few practical rules:

  • structure should serve delivery, not merely mimic layout
  • section hierarchy should stay as stable as possible within one document
  • image assets should remain traceable to their original context
  • one delivery package should support reading, extraction, and review together

docs.title: Known Boundaries
docs.text:
When using Designer, keep in mind:

  • it depends on upstream quality and cannot replace pre-cleaning
  • for semantically unstable sections, it favors overall usability over overly fine labels
  • final business schemas may still require an extra mapping layer

docs.title: Relationship with Processor
docs.text: Designer is not an isolated module. It relies on the stable input prepared by Processor and turns that quality-ready content into delivery directories and structured results for downstream users.

docs.title: Positioning
docs.text:
Processor is the quality-preparation module in PorosData. It does not create the final structured delivery package. Instead, it turns upstream parser outputs into cleaner, more stable intermediate data that downstream workflows can trust.

In short:

  • Processor answers whether the source content is clean and stable enough to keep moving
  • Designer answers how that content should be organized into final deliverables

docs.title: What It Handles
docs.text:
Processor is designed for recurring issues such as:

  • OCR noise, broken spacing, and fragmented numbers
  • Corrupted terms, material names, units, and chemical expressions
  • Noisy captions, table titles, and footnotes
  • Citation, formula, and context boundaries that became unstable after parsing

docs.title: Typical Inputs
docs.text:
Processor usually works from upstream parser results such as:

  • body text blocks
  • figure captions and table titles
  • image-related metadata
  • content-list style files such as *_content_list.json

docs.title: Typical Outputs
docs.text:
Standard outputs are usually written to data/processed/, including:

  • cleaned content lists
  • reusable copies of image assets
  • a batch report such as processing_report.json
  • review-oriented quality checks and suspicious-pattern clues

This layer is still an intermediate stage, but it strongly determines how reliable later structured outputs will be.

docs.title: What Users Gain
docs.text:
After Processor, users typically get:

  • clearer numbers, units, and formula boundaries
  • more stable terms and material names
  • captions and footnotes that are easier to extract from
  • text that is better suited for training, retrieval, and rule-based processing

docs.title: Scope of Cleaning
docs.text:
Processor is not limited to main body text. It also covers key metadata fields such as:

  • text
  • image_caption
  • image_footnote
  • table_caption
  • table_footnote

This helps keep the main text and figure-related content under the same quality standard before the next stage.

docs.title: Typical Repairs
docs.text: Type Common Problem Target Result Numerical repair 0 . 0 1 0 n m 0.010nm Element repair N i Ni Line-break repair 110 \\n s 110s Term normalization Zr based / Zr-based keep one stable form within the document Citation normalization [2,3], [1-3] normalize into one stable protocol

docs.title: Recommended Environment
docs.text:
• Linux is preferred for long-running batch jobs
  • Python 3.8+
  • SSD or NVMe is recommended for routine batch runs
  • No GPU is required

docs.title: Reference Sizing
docs.text: Scenario Suggested Setup Small validation 4 vCPU / 16 GB RAM Routine batch processing 8 vCPU / 32 GB RAM Large long-running jobs 16 vCPU / 64 GB RAM

docs.title: Usage Recommendations
docs.text:
• Prioritize stability for routine batch cleaning
  • Run extra evaluation features separately when needed for spot checks or audits
  • Reduce concurrency when many very long documents are involved

docs.title: Runtime Expectations
docs.text:
Processor is typically CPU-bound. Overall runtime is mostly affected by:

  • document length and formula complexity
  • worker count
  • optional evaluation features
  • whether the environment is Windows or Linux

If logs continue to show progress and reports keep updating, the job is usually still healthy even when a few files take longer than expected.

docs.title: Review and Acceptance Loop
docs.text:
For external delivery projects, Processor should support more than one cleaning pass. A practical quality loop looks like this:

  1. run the batch and produce standard intermediate outputs
  2. review the outputs and identify suspicious patterns or residual issues
  3. improve the correction strategy for recurring problems
  4. rerun and review again until the results are stable enough for delivery

This makes the product easier to use in real delivery scenarios and helps reduce repeated noise over time.

docs.title: Known Boundaries
docs.text:
When using Processor, keep in mind:

  • it does not build the final structured schema
  • it does not replace business-level field design
  • for highly complex formulas or layouts, it favors structural safety over aggressive rewriting

docs.title: Relationship with Designer
docs.text: The more stable the Processor output is, the more reliable the Designer delivery becomes. It should be treated as the quality gate of the delivery chain, not as the final product layer.

docs.title: 简介
docs.text:
PorosData 是面向科研文献的数据处理与结构化交付框架，用于把 PDF、OCR 与解析结果整理成可复查、可复用、可进一步消费的数据资产。

对于材料科学等实证研究场景，原始文献往往包含断裂数字、异常空格、术语误写、公式损坏和图文引用脱节等问题。这些问题会直接影响模型训练、结构化抽取、检索入库和人工复核。PorosData 的目标，就是把这些上游噪音收敛为稳定、清晰、可追溯的交付结果。

docs.title: 适用场景
docs.text:
PorosData 适合放在“原始论文进入可消费数据资产”之间的整理环节。

  • 将科研论文整理为可用于训练的数据文本
  • 为结构化抽取、规则处理和语义检索准备稳定输入
  • 将正文、图注、表题和图片资产组织成统一的交付目录
  • 为后续数据库建设、知识组织和多模态利用提供标准化基础

docs.title: 核心价值
docs.text:
PorosData 以 学术原子性 为原则，强调在提高可用性的同时保留科学表达的完整性。

docs.text:
本页从对外交付视角说明 PorosData 的路线图，重点回答两个问题：

  • 当前产品今天已经能交付什么
  • 最终交付包会如何逐步扩展

docs.title: 功能框架
docs.text:
PorosData 围绕一条连续的交付链路组织能力：

模块 当前角色 主要输出 Parser 接收原始文献与上游解析结果 可继续处理的文本块、图片与基础元数据 Processor 负责质量整理 清洗后的中间结果、处理报告、稳定输入 Designer 负责结构化交付 全文结果、结构化 JSON、多模态索引

这三层不是孤立功能，而是一套面向最终交付的协同框架：先保留原始输入，再稳定内容质量，最后组织成可复用结果。

docs.title: 最终交付包
docs.text:
目标交付包包括：

  • 按文档编号组织的结果目录
  • 面向训练准备的纯文本输出
  • 面向抽取、检索和入库的结构化输出
  • 保持图文引用关联的多模态索引
  • 支持复核与追溯的报告

docs.title: 阶段一：当前可交付能力
docs.text:
当前阶段重点是让整条流水线具备批量使用能力：

  • 从原始文献到最终交付目录的端到端处理
  • 全文结果、结构化结果和多模态索引三类核心输出
  • 标准化的 raw -> processed -> structured 目录模型
  • 基础审计、校验和批处理报告支持
  • 初步形成 process -> review -> correction -> rerun 的交付闭环

docs.title: 阶段二：短期完善方向
docs.text:
短期目标是让输出更稳定，也更容易进入生产项目：

  • 进一步统一术语、单位、引文和章节组织
  • 提升长文档、复杂公式和大批量任务下的稳定性
  • 补充面向外部用户的部署说明、使用说明和结果解读文档
  • 强化图文关联与复核工作流
  • 逐步固化异常模式反馈与规则更新机制

docs.title: 阶段三：最终产品形态
docs.text:
最终目标是形成更完整的科学文献交付产品：

  • 更清晰的批量交付标准与结果验收口径
  • 围绕全文、结构化和多模态输出的一致交付模型
  • 面向训练、抽取、检索和入库的稳定结果复用
  • 更好的项目级跟踪、复核与持续迭代

  • 构建训练语料的工程团队
  • 从事结构化抽取和语义检索的应用团队

docs.title: 设计哲学
docs.text: PorosData 的核心思想很简单：科研文献不是普通文本，而是带有术语、单位、公式、图表和上下文关系的专业内容。系统的价值，不在于把它们“改写得更像自然语言”，而在于把它们整理得更稳定、更清晰、更适合后续使用。

docs.title: 核心支柱一：学术原子性
docs.text: PorosData 将每一份科研内容视为不可随意拆散的学术单元。任何处理动作，都应尽量保留原始语义、物理约束和上下文关系。

docs.title: 字符层
docs.text: 公式、化学式和特殊符号不应因为处理步骤而发生结构性破坏。

docs.title: 关系层
docs.text: 数值、单位、实验条件和结论之间的对应关系不应在清洗或重组中丢失。

docs.title: 结构层
docs.text: 章节层级、图文引用和关键上下文应在最终结果中仍然可追踪、可理解。

docs.title: 核心支柱二：知识约束
docs.text: PorosData 不把科研文本看作纯粹的字符串集合，而是结合领域知识做判断和整理。

docs.title: 规则要服务语义
docs.text: 术语统一、单位规范、引文整理和化学式保护，都是为了让结果更接近科研原意，而不是仅仅追求格式整齐。

docs.title: 经验要能落地
docs.text: 领域经验需要被转成可复用的处理策略，让系统在批量处理时保持相对稳定的判断标准。

docs.title: 核心支柱三：分层交付
docs.text: PorosData 采用分层链路组织交付，而不是把所有问题堆在同一步骤里完成。

docs.title: Parser
docs.text: 尽量完整地保留原始文献中的可用内容和资产。

docs.title: Processor
docs.text: 先解决质量问题，让文本、图注和关键字段达到稳定可用状态。

docs.title: Designer
docs.text: 再把稳定输入组织成全文结果、结构化结果和多模态结果，面向最终交付。

docs.title: 愿景
docs.text: PorosData 希望建立一条面向科研文献的数据交付链路，让原始论文可以更顺畅地进入训练、抽取、检索和复核等实际场景，同时保留学术表达应有的严谨性。

docs.title: 术语表
docs.text: 本页汇总 PorosData 文档中反复出现的核心术语，帮助读者在工作流、工具页和交付说明之间保持统一理解。

docs.title: Parser
docs.text: 上游提取阶段，用于把原始论文转换为可继续处理的文本块、图片、图注和基础元数据。

docs.title: Processor
docs.text: 质量整理阶段，用于清理解析结果中的噪音，使内容达到后续可用状态。

docs.title: Designer
docs.text: 结构化交付阶段，用于把稳定输入组织成全文结果、结构化 JSON 和多模态索引。

docs.title: raw
docs.text: 源数据层，用于保留原始论文和上游解析结果，便于追溯与复查。

docs.title: processed
docs.text: 中间结果层，用于存放清洗后的输出和处理报告。

docs.title: structured
docs.text: 最终交付层，用于存放全文结果、结构化结果和多模态资产。

docs.title: full_text
docs.text: 面向阅读和人工复核的全文交付形式。

docs.title: datamining
docs.text: 面向结构化抽取、检索和入库的交付形式。

docs.title: multimodal
docs.text: 面向图文关联的交付形式，用于把正文中的图表引用与实际图片资产对应起来。

docs.title: doc_id
docs.text: 文档编号，用于组织输出目录并保持交付结构一致。

docs.title: Caption
docs.text: 图或表附带的说明文字，通常也是后续复核和抽取的重要信息来源。

docs.title: Asset Anchor
docs.text: 用于把正文中的图表引用稳定连接到实际资产文件的索引关系。

docs.title: processing_report
docs.text: 批处理摘要文件，用于记录输出状态、运行进度和质量复核线索。

docs.title: 学术原子性
docs.text: 一种处理原则，强调在整理过程中尽量保留科研内容的原始语义、结构线索与上下文关系。

docs.title: PorosData 工作流：从原始论文到最终交付结果
docs.text: 本页说明 PorosData 如何把原始科研文献整理为可用于训练、结构化抽取、检索和人工复核的标准化结果。重点不是单个函数调用，而是用户如何理解整条交付链路。

docs.title: 整体流程
docs.text:
原始文献 -> Parser -> Processor -> Designer -> 最终交付目录

阶段 主要任务 交付结果 Parser 提取正文、图表、图注和基础元数据 可继续处理的原始内容与图片资源 Processor 清理噪音、修复断裂、统一表达 高质量中间结果与处理报告 Designer 组织章节、生成结构化视图与索引 全文结果、结构化 JSON、多模态结果

docs.title: 输入与输出目录
docs.text:
PorosData 推荐按三层目录组织数据：

data/
├── raw/          # 上游原始结果
├── processed/    # 清洗后的中间结果
└── structured/   # 最终交付目录

数据流向为 raw -> processed -> structured。

docs.title: 阶段 1：原始输入进入 raw
docs.text:
raw 层保存上游解析结果和原始图片资源，典型内容包括：

  • 原始 PDF
  • 解析得到的 Markdown 或内容列表
  • 页面级中间文件
  • 从文献中切出的图片资源

这一层的目标不是直接交付，而是完整保留上游输入，方便追溯和复查。

docs.title: 阶段 2：Processor 生成 processed
docs.text:
Processor 负责把原始内容整理成稳定、清晰、可继续消费的中间结果。这里通常会处理以下问题：

  • 数字、小数点和单位被异常空格打断
  • 术语、材料名和化学式出现断裂或误写
  • 图注、表题和脚注中存在明显噪音
  • 长文本中混入控制字符、格式残影和无意义碎片

这一阶段的标准交付通常包括：

  • 清洗后的 *_content_list.json
  • 图片资源的可复用拷贝
  • processing_report.json 形式的处理报告

docs.title: 阶段 3：Designer 生成 structured
docs.text:
Designer 在高质量输入基础上组织最终交付结果。常见输出包括：

data/structured/
├── full_text/
├── datamining/
└── multimodal/

其中三类结果分别面向不同用途：

目录 作用 常见文件 full_text/ 交付可阅读、可复核的全文结果 _structured.json, _structured.txt datamining/ 交付适合抽取、检索和入库的结构化结果 _datamining.json multimodal/ 交付图文关联清晰的索引与图片资产 _index.json, fig_*.md, assets/

docs.title: 用户最终会得到什么
docs.text:
完成一轮标准处理后，用户通常会获得以下结果：

  1. 一套按文档编号组织的交付目录
  2. 一份适合训练使用的纯文本结果
  3. 一份适合抽取和检索的结构化结果
  4. 一套可用于图文联动的多模态索引
  5. 一份可用于批处理复盘的处理报告

docs.title: 典型使用顺序
docs.text:
对于批量项目，推荐按以下顺序理解和使用结果：

  1. 先查看 raw/ 是否完整，确认原始输入没有缺失
  2. 再检查 processed/ 的处理报告，确认清洗阶段是否稳定完成
  3. 最后进入 structured/，按具体用途读取全文、结构化结果或多模态索引

  • 为图表与正文联动准备可索引资产
  • 为后续数据库建设或知识组织提供统一交付目录

docs.text:

  • 可写入的本地环境或虚拟环境
  • 足够容纳原始数据、中间结果和最终结果的磁盘空间

docs.title: 清洗文本
docs.text:
使用 TextCleaner 标准化科学文本，同时保留数学公式的完整性：

from porosdata_processor import TextCleaner

# 初始化默认设置的清洗器
cleaner = TextCleaner()

# 处理文本
raw_text = "The energy equation is $E = mc^2$, involving α particles and β rays."
cleaned_text = cleaner.clean(raw_text)

print(cleaned_text)
# 输出: "The energy equation is $E = mc^2$, involving \alpha particles and \beta rays."

docs.title: 自定义流水线
docs.text:
配置带有特定插件的清洗器：

# 创建带有特定插件的清洗器
cleaner = TextCleaner(pipeline=[
    "citation_rules",      # 标准化引用
    "greek_to_latex",      # 转换希腊字母
    "normalize_whitespace" # 清理间距
])

text = "See reference 【1】 for α particle data."
result = cleaner.clean(text)
# 输出: "See reference [1] for \alpha particle data."

docs.title: 高级选项
docs.text:
启用高级 LaTeX 公式清洗功能：

# 启用高级 LaTeX 公式清洗
cleaner = TextCleaner(clean_options={
    "clean_latex_math_spaces": True  # 移除公式内的额外空格
})

text = "Formula: $\\mathbf { X } + \\frac { a }{ b }$"
result = cleaner.clean(text)
# 输出: "Formula: $\\mathbf{X} + \\frac{a}{b}$"

docs.title: 处理单个文件
docs.text:
# 清洗 Markdown 文件
cleaner.clean_file(
    input_path="document.md",
    output_path="clean_document.md",
    encoding="utf-8"
)

docs.title: 批量处理
docs.text:
from processing.batch_processor import BatchProcessor

processor = BatchProcessor()
processor.process_text_data(
    input_dir="data/raw",
    output_dir="data/cleaned"
)

docs.title: 处理配置
docs.text:
创建 config/processing_config.yaml：

cleaning:
  convert_greek: true
  apply_rules: true
  apply_patterns: true
  normalize_whitespace: true
  remove_extra_spaces: true

processing:
  concurrency: 0  # 0 表示顺序处理
  verbose: true

docs.title: Token 配置
docs.text:
对于高级分词设置，创建 config/token_config.yaml：

model_type: "llama"  # 或 "gpt", "custom"

tokens:
  llama:
    bos: "<s>"
    eos: "</s>"
    inst_start: "[INST]"
    inst_end: "[/INST]"

splitting:
  max_chunk_tokens: 512
  split_by_paragraph: true
  preserve_paragraphs: true
  overlap_tokens: 50

docs.text:

docs.title: 本页范围
docs.text:
当前仓库文档主要围绕处理层展开。对外最常用的入口可分为四类：

范围 负责内容 常见入口 Processor 文本清洗与质量整理 TextCleaner、CLI run 批处理 将多篇文献整理为 processed 结果 python -m porosdata_processor run 复核与验收 在交付前检查中间结果 audit、delivery-gate 一类命令 Designer 交接 将稳定的 processed 结果转入最终交付 作为下游阶段存在，不是本页主要代码接口

如果你正在寻找最终结构化交付结果，请在完成处理阶段后继续阅读 Designer 文档。

docs.text:
最常见的使用路径是：

原始论文或上游解析结果
-> TextCleaner 或批处理命令
-> processed 中间结果
-> 复核与验收
-> 下游结构化交付

docs.title: TextCleaner
docs.text: 当你希望在 Python 代码里清洗单段科研文本时，优先使用 TextCleaner。

docs.title: 构造函数
docs.text:
TextCleaner(pipeline=None, clean_options=None)
参数 类型 含义 pipeline list | None 清洗插件的执行顺序 clean_options dict | None 额外的清洗开关

docs.title: 异常与失败信号
docs.text:
Python API 在配置不正确或处理失败时，可能抛出以下两类常见异常：

异常 含义 常见原因 ProcessingError 处理失败 输入异常、特殊文本情况或运行失败 ConfigurationError 配置无效 参数结构错误或配置值不支持 
try:
    cleaner = TextCleaner()
    result = cleaner.clean(text)
except ProcessingError as e:
    print(f"处理失败: {e}")
except ConfigurationError as e:
    print(f"配置错误: {e}")

对于批处理任务，更多失败信号通常出现在日志、处理报告和交付验收结果中，而不是直接体现在单个 Python 异常里。

Research Note / 研发手记

本篇文档属于 PorosData 研究与思考 系列，主要记录架构演进、尚未正式落地的算法推演和科学数据处理中的开放问题。它不代表框架最终的稳定功能承诺。

docs.title: 设计洞察
docs.text:
快速链接： 首页 | 快速开始

为了确保数据能够真正用于模型训练与科学数据挖掘，PorosData 在数据处理过程中强调语义稳定性、结构一致性与可挖掘性。

针对不同的使用场景，数据质量的要求也有所不同。其中最核心的两类应用场景分别为：

  • 大模型预训练（Pre-training）：学习世界知识与语言结构
  • 自动化数据挖掘（Data Mining）：从海量文献中提取结构化知识

docs.title: 文档落位
docs.text:
本页承担研究性总览与技术路径讨论，而具体的工程约束已分别沉淀到现有框架中的两个工具页：

  • Processor：见 tools/processor/index.md，聚焦数据质量交付、清洗标准与接入 Designer 的前置条件
  • Designer：见 tools/designer/index.md，聚焦结构化视图、Poros 标签契约与数据挖掘交付标准

docs.title: 1. 数据清洗能力（PorosData Processor）
docs.text:
在大模型预训练阶段，文本数据以 token 序列的形式被模型读取，其核心目标是让模型学习世界知识以及语言结构。如果原始数据中包含错误或噪声，模型便可能在训练过程中形成错误的统计关联，进而影响其对科学概念的理解。因此，面向训练准备的数据在进入预训练流程前必须满足三个基本要求：token 纯净、术语准确以及文本结构连贯。

首先，数据需要保证token 流的纯净性。在许多由 PDF 或 OCR 转换而来的文本中，往往会混入与语义无关的字符，例如控制符号、页码索引或格式残留。这些符号并不参与语法结构或语义表达，但在语言模型训练中却会被当作普通 token 处理，从而干扰模型对上下文概率分布的学习。因此，需要对这些非语义字符进行检测与清理，使最终的文本 token 流仅包含与内容相关的信息。

其次，数据需要保证 科学术语的语义准确性。科学文献中的术语具有高度稳定的语义结构，如果在文本解析过程中发生系统性误识，模型将学习到错误的知识。例如，在 OCR 处理中，X-ray 可能被误识为 10-ray，这种错误不仅改变了字符形式，还破坏了原有的科学概念。一旦这类错误在训练数据中大量存在，模型在后续任务中就可能无法正确理解与射线衍射相关的科学语境。因此，数据需要通过术语词典与上下文规则确保关键科学概念不会被错误替换。

最后，数据还需要保证 长文本结构的连贯性。在 PDF 文档解析过程中，跨行断词与连字符丢失是常见问题。例如 short-range 可能被拆分为 short - range，甚至在换行处被截断为 shortrange。这类结构错误会增加模型词表的不确定性，使本应稳定的术语被拆解为多个无意义 token，从而增加语言建模的复杂度。数据处理需要通过修复断词与恢复连字符来保证文本在 token 层面的结构一致性，从而提高模型对复杂长句的理解能力。

docs.title: 2. 数据结构化能力（PorosData Designer）
docs.text:
与预训练任务不同，数据挖掘的目标是从海量科学文献中自动提取结构化知识，例如材料成分、实验条件或物理参数。在这一场景下，数据质量的关键不再是语言流畅性，而是实体识别的稳定性、数值表达的准确性以及图文信息之间的对齐关系。

首先，数据需要保证数值与单位表达的确定性。科学文献中的关键知识往往以数值形式出现，例如温度、压力或材料参数。然而在 OCR 解析过程中，指数表达式和数字序列常常被错误拆分，例如 \(10^5\) 可能被解析为 \(1 0 ^ { 5 }\)。这种结构破坏会使自动化挖掘算法无法识别正确的数量级，从而导致属性提取失败。因此，数据处理流程需要对科学计数法和指数结构进行恢复，使数值表达保持标准化形式。

其次，数据需要保证实体识别的稳定性。在材料科学文献中，大量关键信息依赖于化学元素和材料名称，例如 Ni、Au 或 Fe3C。如果这些实体在文本解析过程中被误识为 LaTeX 符号或其他字符结构，例如将 Au 解析为 \Au，则后续的实体识别（NER）与实体链接（Entity Linking）都会受到影响，最终导致知识图谱中的实体节点无法正确建立。因此，数据处理流程需要通过规则与词典保护关键科学实体，使其在解析与结构化过程中保持一致。

最后，数据还需要保证多模态资产的锚定能力。科学文献中的重要信息往往不仅存在于正文中，还体现在图表与图像数据中。传统文本解析通常只保留“Fig. 1”或“Table 2”这样的字符串引用，但不会建立文本与图像之间的直接关联。数据处理流程需要把这些引用转换为可索引的结构化锚点，使文本中的图表引用能够直接定位到对应的图像资产与说明文字（caption）。这种图文之间的结构化连接是实现多模态知识挖掘与科学文档理解的重要基础。

docs.title: 科研数据处理技术路径全景图
1. 正则匹配（Regex）：底层「清道夫」
docs.text: 维度 说明 核心逻辑 基于模式匹配的硬编码规则 适用场景 物理量连词（3 m m → 3mm）、小数点断裂（0 . 1 → 0.1）、页码/页眉噪声剔除 优点 速度极快（微秒级）、确定性 100%、不消耗算力 缺点 无法处理歧义。例如 Ni- 后面若是换行需连起来，若在句尾可能是负号，正则难以判断 贡献 初步提升信噪比，减少无意义的 Token 浪费

docs.title: 2. 词语表挂载（Glossary/Dictionary）：领域知识「防线」
docs.text: 维度 说明 核心逻辑 利用 Aho-Corasick 等算法进行多模式匹配，将 OCR 碎字符强制对齐到专业术语 适用场景 化学元素（Z r → Zr）、材料缩写（B M G → BMG）、专业仪器 优点 极大解决「实体断裂」问题，通过外挂术语表保证核心数据准确性 缺点 维护成本高，对不在词表内的「新材料」或「复合材料」无能为力 Data Mining 贡献 确保实体统一，是构建知识图谱（KG）和属性抽取的核心前提

docs.title: 3. OCR 模型选配：源头「降维打击」
docs.text: 维度 说明 核心逻辑 从传统「文字识别」转向「视觉语义理解」 代表工具 传统 OCR（PaddleOCR、Tesseract）：逐字识别，科学公式和化学符号易崩坏，产生大量 \mathbf 噪声；视觉公式模型（Nougat、Marker）：针对学术 PDF，不识别单字，直接预测 Markdown/LaTeX 序列 优点 完美还原复杂表格、数学公式和多栏布局 缺点 对算力有要求，非标排版文档可能产生幻觉（如漏段） 贡献 直接输出结构化文本，跳过约 80% 的正则清洗工作

docs.title: 4. 小模型微调/润色（SLM Finetuning）：语义「终极纠正」
docs.text: 维度 说明 核心逻辑 利用 1B–3B 规模模型（如 Qwen、Llama），通过 Prompt 或 SFT（指令微调）进行语义纠错 适用场景 处理 \Delta Nb 等复杂的、非固定模式的 OCR 伪影 优点 具备「常识」，能推断 Ni 后大概率跟 Nb 而非生僻符号 缺点 速度较慢，需控制不改变原文含义（只改错、不重写） 贡献 将文本质量提升至接近正式出版物的水平，利于向量检索和后续利用

docs.title: 技术方案对比总结
docs.text: 方案 处理成本 灵活性 准确度 核心目标 正则匹配 极低 低（Hardcode） 极高（针对模式） 消除物理噪声（空格、格式） 词表挂载 低 中（依赖更新） 100%（词表内） 实体对齐（材料名、化学式） OCR 选配 中/高 高 高（针对 PDF） 结构化还原（公式、表格） SLM 微调 高 极高 极高（带语义） 终极语义纠正

docs.title: 问题背景
docs.text:
科研文献包含术语、数值、公式、图表和上下文限定语。一旦论文从 PDF 或 OCR 结果转换为可处理文本，很多看似细小的格式问题都会迅速放大成下游数据问题。

常见问题包括：

  • 数字和单位被拆散
  • 科学术语被误写
  • 公式边界受损
  • 图注和图表引用失去对应关系
  • 温度、条件、方法等上下文从对应数值旁边漂移开

因此，科研数据准备不能沿用普通文本处理的质量标准，而需要更贴近专业内容本身的判断方式。

docs.title: 为什么训练准备和数据挖掘的要求不同
docs.text: 这两类下游场景关注的问题并不相同。

docs.title: 1. 训练准备
docs.text:
训练准备更关注序列质量和语义连续性。

  • Token 纯净度：控制字符、页码残留和其他非语义碎片会浪费序列长度，并干扰学习。
  • 术语准确性：像 X-ray -> 10-ray 这样的术语损坏，会直接把错误概念带入训练数据。
  • 长文本连贯性：断词、连字符缺失和标点损坏，会降低长段科学文本的稳定性。

docs.title: 2. 数据挖掘
docs.text:
数据挖掘更关注结构精度和上下文绑定关系。

  • 数值与单位 必须保持确定，否则后续抽取无法识别正确数量级。
  • 实体名称 必须保持稳定，否则匹配、链接和归一化都会变得不可靠。
  • 图文锚点 必须保持明确，否则图片和图注难以进入结构化交付。

docs.title: PorosData 的落点
docs.text:
PorosData 通过分层交付链路同时覆盖这两类场景：

阶段 主要职责 为什么重要 Parser 保留可继续利用的源内容和资产 让原始输入尽量完整进入后续流程 Processor 去噪并稳定文本质量 为后续使用准备可靠中间结果 Designer 导出可交付结构 将稳定输入组织成全文、结构化和多模态结果

也就是说，PorosData 不把“清洗”和“交付”看成完全割裂的两件事，而是把它们放在一条从原始文献到可复用结果的连续路径上。

docs.title: 我们需要什么样的数据质量？
docs.text: 目标质量可以概括为两个视角。

docs.title: 训练准备视角
docs.text:
• 文本应清晰、可读、结构连续
  • 科学术语应保持语义正确
  • 公式和行内引用应尽量保持完整，便于后续使用

docs.title: 数据挖掘视角
docs.text:
• 数值、单位和属性应保持可识别
  • 实体在文档内外应尽量稳定
  • 图表引用、图注和其他元数据应与正文保持关联

docs.title: 当前限制与开放问题
docs.text:
即使流程已经较稳定，仍然存在一些开放问题：

  • 自动修复应推进到什么程度，才不会反过来改变原始语义
  • 对极不规则的公式，应如何整理而不破坏结构
  • 领域词表的覆盖度需要达到什么水平，维护成本才仍然可控
  • 在不同解析器输出之间，如何保持图文锚定的一致性

这些问题并不仅仅是实现细节，它们会直接影响交付包能否在不同项目中持续复用。

docs.title: 延伸阅读
docs.text:

  • Processor

  • API 参考

docs.title: 定位
docs.text:
Designer 是 PorosData 中负责结构化交付的模块。它建立在 Processor 已完成质量整理的基础上，把文本、图表和上下文组织为适合训练、抽取、检索和复核使用的最终结果。

简而言之：

  • Processor 负责把内容整理干净
  • Designer 负责把内容组织成可交付结果

docs.title: 主要职责
docs.text:
Designer 重点处理以下工作：

  • 章节与段落重组
  • 结构化字段组织
  • 图文资产关联
  • 全文结果与结构化结果导出
  • 多模态索引生成

它不承担大规模 OCR 清洗，而是把已经稳定的中间结果进一步变成可交付产品。

docs.title: 三类核心产物
docs.text:
当前 Designer 主要输出三类结果：

产物 面向用途 常见文件 全文结果 阅读、复核、训练准备 _structured.txt, _structured.json 结构化结果 抽取、检索、入库 _datamining.json 多模态结果 图文联动、图片索引、资产管理 _index.json, fig_*.md, assets/

docs.title: 输出目录
docs.text:
典型输出目录如下：

data/structured/
├── full_text/{doc_id}/
├── datamining/{doc_id}/
└── multimodal/{doc_id}/

每个文档按 doc_id 独立存放，便于批处理交付、抽查和回溯。

docs.title: 用户能获得什么
docs.text:
在标准交付中，Designer 会把同一篇文献整理为多种可复用结果：

  • 一份可直接阅读的全文结果
  • 一份适合训练使用的纯文本流
  • 一份适合结构化抽取和检索的 JSON 结果
  • 一套图文引用关系清晰的多模态索引

docs.title: full_text
docs.text:
full_text 面向全文交付，通常包含：

  • 带结构标记的完整文本
  • 去除结构标记后的纯文本流
  • 便于人工审阅的文本版本

docs.title: datamining
docs.text:
datamining 面向结构化利用，通常包含：

  • 标题
  • 章节内容
  • 公式列表
  • 化学式或材料式
  • 图表引用信息

docs.title: multimodal
docs.text:
multimodal 面向图文联动，通常包含：

  • 图片索引文件
  • 按图拆分的说明卡片
  • 与正文引用对应的图片资产

docs.title: 输入要求
docs.text:
为了得到稳定结果，Designer 依赖以下前置条件：

  • 文本中的主要噪音已经在上一步处理完成
  • 数值、单位、术语和材料名具备较好一致性
  • 图注、表题、脚注等关键字段可直接使用
  • 正文与图表的引用关系没有被上游破坏

docs.title: 设计原则
docs.text:
Designer 的组织方式遵循以下原则：

  • 结构优先服务交付，而不是复刻排版
  • 同一文档的章节层级应尽量稳定
  • 图文资产要能回到原始上下文
  • 一套结果应同时支持阅读、抽取和复查

docs.title: 已知边界
docs.text:
使用 Designer 时需要注意：

  • 它依赖上游输入质量，无法替代前置清洗
  • 对语义极不稳定的章节，不追求过细标签，而优先保证整体可用
  • 最终字段设计仍应结合具体业务需求做二次映射

docs.title: 与 Processor 的关系
docs.text: Designer 不是单独工作的模块。它建立在 Processor 提供的稳定输入之上，负责把质量结果进一步转换成面向最终使用者的交付目录和结构化成果。

docs.title: 定位
docs.text:
Processor 是 PorosData 中负责质量整理的模块。它的任务不是生成最终结构化结果，而是把上游解析输出整理成稳定、清晰、可继续处理的中间数据，为后续结构化和批量利用打好基础。

简而言之：

  • Processor 解决“原始内容是否足够干净、稳定、可继续使用”
  • Designer 解决“这些内容如何组织成最终交付结果”

docs.title: 适合处理什么问题
docs.text:
Processor 主要面向以下典型问题：

  • OCR 造成的异常空格、断词和断裂数字
  • 材料名、术语、单位和化学式的误写或碎裂
  • 图注、表题、脚注中的噪音和格式残留
  • 引文、公式和上下文锚点在解析后变得不稳定

docs.title: 输入内容
docs.text:
Processor 通常接收来自上游解析阶段的原始结果，例如：

  • 正文文本块
  • 图注与表题
  • 图片相关元数据
  • *_content_list.json 一类内容列表文件

docs.title: 输出内容
docs.text:
标准输出通常写入 data/processed/，包括：

  • 清洗后的内容列表
  • 可复用的图片资源副本
  • 批处理报告，如 processing_report.json
  • 面向复核的质量检查结果与异常模式线索

这一步的结果仍然属于中间层，不直接承担最终交付展示，但会直接决定后续结构化结果的稳定性。

docs.title: 用户能获得什么
docs.text:
使用 Processor 后，用户通常会得到以下改进：

  • 数字、单位和公式边界更清晰
  • 术语与材料名称更稳定
  • 图注、表题和脚注更适合后续抽取
  • 文本更适合训练、检索和规则处理

docs.title: 处理范围
docs.text:
Processor 不只处理正文，也覆盖关键元数据字段，例如：

  • text
  • image_caption
  • image_footnote
  • table_caption
  • table_footnote

这样做的目的是保证正文与图表信息在进入下游之前保持同一质量标准。

docs.title: 典型清理内容
docs.text: 类型 常见问题 目标结果 数值修复 0 . 0 1 0 n m 0.010nm 元素修复 N i Ni 行内碎裂修复 110 \\n s 110s 术语统一 Zr based / Zr-based 同文档内尽量统一 引文整理 [2,3], [1-3] 统一为稳定协议

docs.title: 推荐环境
docs.text:
• Linux 服务器优先
  • Python 3.8+
  • 常规批量建议使用 SSD 或 NVMe
  • 不需要 GPU

docs.title: 参考配置
docs.text: 场景 建议配置 小规模验证 4 vCPU / 16 GB RAM 常规批处理 8 vCPU / 32 GB RAM 长时大批量运行 16 vCPU / 64 GB RAM

docs.title: 推荐使用方式
docs.text:
• 日常批量清洗优先关注稳定性
  • 评估类附加功能建议在抽检或审计阶段单独开启
  • 长文档较多时，适当降低并行度通常更稳妥

docs.title: 运行时表现
docs.text:
Processor 是典型的 CPU 密集型流程。整体耗时通常受到以下因素影响：

  • 文档长度和公式复杂度
  • 并行 worker 数量
  • 是否开启额外评估统计
  • 当前运行环境是 Windows 还是 Linux

如果日志持续推进、处理报告不断更新，通常说明任务在正常运行，而不一定是卡住。

docs.title: 质量复核机制
docs.text:
对于对外交付项目，Processor 不只负责清洗，还应支持持续复核。推荐将这一阶段理解为一个逐步收敛的质量闭环：

  1. 完成批量处理，形成标准中间结果
  2. 对结果进行质量检查，识别可疑模式和残留问题
  3. 对高频问题补充修正策略
  4. 重新处理并再次复核，直到结果达到可交付状态

这种机制更适合外部项目中的稳定交付，也有助于持续减少重复性噪音问题。

docs.title: 已知边界
docs.text:
使用 Processor 时需要注意：

  • 它不负责最终目录建模或知识组织
  • 它不会替代人工定义业务字段
  • 对结构极其复杂的公式和版式，优先保证不破坏原始结构，而不是激进改写

docs.title: 与 Designer 的关系
docs.text: Processor 的输出越稳定，Designer 的结构化结果越可靠。推荐把它视为交付链路中的质量入口，而不是最终结果本身。
